mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST falls by >10% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when both GDPC1 and HOUST meet the stated thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below the previous year's minimum for three consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which tends to precede negative equity returns as profit margins erode over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < min(INDPRO last 12 months) for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of three consecutive monthly INDPRO minima.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 units, combined with a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a labor market mismatch; this typically precedes negative equity returns over the next 5 trading days due to uncertainty and hiring inefficiencies.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when both PAYEMS > 100,000 and UNRATE rises simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for six consecutive months signals a deflationary environment, which increases real discount rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of six consecutive months with CPIAUCSL < 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a synchronized demand expansion, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when both GDPC1 and HOUST exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between industrial production growth (INDPRO) and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days; rising industrial output signals improved supply capacity and earnings momentum.
failure_condition: The correlation between monthly INDPRO growth and subsequent 5-day S&P 500 returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample tests.
